title: Someone who does or is something

blocks.text: Someone who does or is something
-тель — -er (a suffix appended to words to create a masculine noun, usually denoting a profession, performer of an action or a human relation)

Wiktionary gives -тель one meaning: “-er (a suffix appended to words to create a masculine noun, usually denoting a profession, performer of an action or a human relation)”. So every word its etymologies build with -тель has it.

head: Word
Made of (Wiktionary's etymology)
Meaning (Wiktionary)
rows: listener, hearer, audience (someone who listens); student

blocks.text: Wiktionary, «-тель» (https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/-тель#Russian): the suffix's only meaning there and in the Russian Wiktionary.
-тель — someone who carries out the action of the base
««тот, кто выполняет указанное в основе действие»» is how the Russian Wiktionary puts this meaning of -тель. Its examples: водитель, носитель, каратель.
Russian Wiktionary, «-тель», meaning 1 (https://ru.wiktionary.org/wiki/-тель).
-ник — someone connected with the activity, profession, tool or material of the base

«тот, кто связан с указанной в основе деятельностью, профессией, орудием или материалом труда» is how the Russian Wiktionary puts this meaning of -ник. Its examples: лесник, грибник, книжник, дворник.
Russian Wiktionary, «-ник», meaning 1 (https://ru.wiktionary.org/wiki/-ник).
-ец — -er, -an, -ian (nominal suffix for agent nouns or nouns designating persons).

-er, -an, -ian (nominal suffix for agent nouns or nouns designating persons). — Аме́рика (“America”) + -е́ц → америка́нец (“American”); боро́ться (“to fight, wrestle”) + -ец → боре́ц (“champion, wrestler”); вдова́ (“widow”) + -ец → вдове́ц (“widower”)

head: Word
Made of (Wiktionary's etymology)
Meaning (Wiktionary)
rows: fool, blockhead, turkey, gander, dummy, dunce, idiot
(historical, or, dated) copyist, penman, scribe, scrivener, writer
(bookish) old man, whitebeard; (christianity) monastic elder, starets

blocks.text: Wiktionary, «-ец» (https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/-ец#Russian).
-ец — someone engaged in the activity of the base
««тот, кто занимается указанной в основе деятельностью»» is how the Russian Wiktionary puts this meaning of -ец. Its examples: творец, певец, лжец, продавец, полководец, баснописец.

head: Word
Made of (Wiktionary's etymology)
Meaning (Wiktionary)
rows: seller, salesman, vendor; shop assistant (shop employee)

blocks.text: Russian Wiktionary, «-ец», meaning 3 (https://ru.wiktionary.org/wiki/-ец).
-ец — someone who carries out the action of the base
««тот, кто выполняет указанное в основе действие»» is how the Russian Wiktionary puts this meaning of -ец. Its examples: кормилец, владелец.
Russian Wiktionary, «-ец», meaning 4 (https://ru.wiktionary.org/wiki/-ец).
-ец — someone who has the property of the base
««тот, кто который обладает указанным в основе свойством»» is how the Russian Wiktionary puts this meaning of -ец. Its examples: глупец, юнец, мертвец.

corpse, cadaver, dead man, dead body

blocks.text: Russian Wiktionary, «-ец», meaning 7 (https://ru.wiktionary.org/wiki/-ец).
-ец — someone belonging to the organisation or community of the base

««тот, кто принадлежит к указанной в основе организации, общности»» is how the Russian Wiktionary puts this meaning of -ец. Its examples: абаканец, украинец, уралец, горец, олимпиец, марафонец, чужеземец, иноверец.
Russian Wiktionary, «-ец», meaning 1 (https://ru.wiktionary.org/wiki/-ец).
-ок — (animate, takes verbs, produces nouns) agent
(animate, takes verbs, produces nouns) agent — е́здить (“to ride”) + -о́к → ездо́к (“rider”); стреля́ть (“to shoot”) + -о́к → стрело́к (“shooter”); знать (“to know”) + -о́к → знато́к (“cognoscente”)
Wiktionary, «-ок» (https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/-ок#Russian).
-щик — Suffix added to nouns, verbs and sometimes adjectives to form masculine agent nouns: -er, -or
Wiktionary gives -щик one meaning: “Suffix added to nouns, verbs and sometimes adjectives to form masculine agent nouns: -er, -or”. So every word its etymologies build with -щик has it.
Wiktionary, «-щик» (https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/-щик#Russian): the suffix's only meaning there and in the Russian Wiktionary.
